section_summary: A Japanese textile manufacturer explains how it printed a design registered by a British firm in Singapore and identifies the buyer, suppliers, and shipment. The remaining documents transmit a December 1949 SCAP rule on marking Japanese exports, together with the rule itself and a press release explaining when buyers may request that origin markings be omitted.

people.name: H. Hamada
people.role: Signatory for Kanegafuchi Spinning Co., Ltd.

people.name: K. B. Bush
people.role: Brigadier General, AGD, and Adjutant General

subfiles.title: Written Explanation on Infringement of Registration of Design
subfiles.to: Chemical and Technical Division, ESS, GHQ
subfiles.about: Kanegafuchi explains its production and shipment of a cotton print bearing a design registered by a British firm.
subfiles.summary: The company says a buyer supplied the design and that it did not know the design was registered; it lists the buyer, suppliers, and Singapore shipment.

subfiles.title: Transmission of SCAP Memorandum for Japanese Government Regarding Marking of Export Articles
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser forwards a SCAP memorandum and press release on marking Japanese exports.
subfiles.summary: The despatch explains the new buyer requested exception to origin marking and notes Japanese press attention to that exception.

subfiles.title: Marking of Export Articles
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: SCAP sets requirements for marking Japanese export goods and permits omission when a buyer certifies that the destination country does not require it.
subfiles.summary: Export goods and packaging must ordinarily bear a conspicuous, durable Japan origin mark. The memorandum also requires action against misleading claims about origin, quantity, quality, or content.

subfiles.title: Modification Is Made of Export Mark Rule
subfiles.about: The release announces that buyers may request omission of Japan origin marks when the destination country does not require them.
subfiles.summary: SCAP announces the marking exception while reaffirming that Japanese goods must not be falsely described as made elsewhere or misrepresented in quantity, quality, or content.
